title: Operations Console Boundary
intent: Expose review operations through a server-enforced API rather than trusted UI state.
problem: Without server APIs enforce tenant and reviewer checks regardless of UI state, the system can accept an outcome that is not justified by the operations console boundary contract.
context: This pattern addresses operators inspect and decide queued work; its concrete control is server APIs enforce tenant and reviewer checks regardless of UI state.
forces: Correctness requires that hidden buttons are never authorization controls
Operational pressure can cause: client-supplied role unlocks an action
solution: Implement server APIs enforce tenant and reviewer checks regardless of UI state. Verify the anchored symbol `ConsolePrincipal` with `test_console_requires_session_and_has_security_headers` before reuse.
invariants: hidden buttons are never authorization controls
failure_modes: cached UI data crosses tenant sessions
security: The security boundary specifically rejects `client-supplied role unlocks an action` and fails closed if the operations console boundary evidence cannot be verified.
privacy: For operations console boundary, persist only its decision identifiers and digests; exclude payload data unrelated to server APIs enforce tenant and reviewer checks regardless of UI state.
reuse_constraints: Confirm the target still requires: operators inspect and decide queued work
Do not apply when: no human operations interface exists
External Ethernian promotion signature remains mandatory
applies_when: operators inspect and decide queued work
